title: Your whole UI. One canvas. Real code.
description: Explore real application screens, states and interactive flows on a zoomable canvas, built and maintained with your coding agent.
eyebrow: App Canvas · Open source · Agent native
tldr: See the implemented UI together: full screens, named conditions and connected flows.
Keep one UI implementation. Your coding agent creates the fixtures, adapter and coverage checks.
Try {states} states and {flows} flows in the public synthetic demo. No login or API key.
tour: See it, use it, play it
features: Zoom out to understand the app
Browse full screens grouped by page. Search, filter and collapse sidebars. Follow a flow link and the camera moves to the destination.
Zoom in to use the real UI
Browse locks controls for safe panning. Select a screen, choose Interact, and use its original application code with disposable synthetic data.
Press Demo to explain a journey
Play happy, failure and recovery flows in a continuing app session, with action cues, captions, pause, speed and a step timeline.

guideTitle: From an existing repo to an interactive canvas
guideIntro: Give the job to an agent that can read and edit your repository and run commands. No existing Storybook or manually prepared screen list is required. Installation alone does not populate the canvas.
promptLabel: Paste this into your coding agent
steps: Use Node.js 22+ and the project's package manager and lockfile. Install the pinned GitHub release, then its browser. On npm 12, add --allow-git=root only if Git admission blocks this direct dependency; do not change global policy.

Run discover on the whole application root. The agent reviews every generated source region and candidate, resolves pending items, and enumerates semantic states independently of the eventual catalog. Keep unresolved blockers visible.
Render the original UI with fixtures

The agent adds ui-review/canvas.config.mjs, a catalog, synthetic fixtures, a preview entry and checked journeys. The web adapter imports real pages, providers and styles; fixtures replace data and dependencies, not the UI. Reject unknown network requests.

Author the implemented normal, empty, loading, error, denied, dialog and recovery conditions. Check every case and run real controls in continuing flows. Reconcile the inventory, source-linked assertions and route coverage, then pass --complete against the same application root.

Run ui:review, inspect the overview and state graph, then play a flow. Ask the agent to edit the actual app source. Existing previews rebuild; new routes and conditions need inventory, fixture and journey updates. Require the complete gate before handover.
filesText: The shared package owns the viewer, CLI and skill. Your repo owns its adapter, fixtures, independent inventory, catalog and interaction checks. Start with the runnable React/Vite reference; use a project-specific adapter for other stacks.
skillText: Codex and Claude Code can install the bundled skill. Any other coding agent can follow AGENT_GUIDE.md directly. The canvas runtime makes no model calls and requires no model API key. Your chosen agent has its own costs and permissions.
limitsTitle: What this release does and does not prove
limits: Web previews use actual HTML/CSS and original JavaScript for interaction. Native UIKit, SwiftUI and Android need original-runtime harnesses and evidence; a capture is not a live native app.
Coverage is a reviewed source-to-case contract, not automatic discovery of every possible business condition. UI checks do not qualify production backends, clinical accuracy or model precision.
Viewer: English by default, with 11 languages. The public demo is a frozen synthetic frontend; live integrations watch your source. Physical iPad performance has not been measured.
story: AI made it easy to build another page. It did not make a growing application easy to understand. I wanted to see the implemented screens and their failure states together without clicking through the whole app or maintaining a second design file.

App Canvas turns that review into a navigable landscape. A coding agent does the repository-specific integration; the shared tool supplies the canvas, original-code web previews, camera-following navigation and checked playback.
StoolSense is the synthetic public example. It has no production session, real health records or AI requests. Optional anonymous tool usage events are separate from app data.
privacy: Synthetic demo · no app backend · no login · no API key
readmeMore: Detailed API, native workflow, alternatives and release maintenance are documented in the English README and agent guide.
